thread:
alex: Quick idea — introduce probabilistic retry sampling at the edge to tame hedging/backpressure amplification. Start with a 5% sampled midstream-retry path and attach sample headers so downstream can dedupe and count.

marta: curious — how is this different from our hedging budget? does sampling bypass circuit-breakers?

alex: sampling is orthogonal. hedging budget stays for deterministic hedges; sampling is an opt-in lightweight retry that doesn't consume the hedging quota. think of it as canary retries to surface flaky hosts without draining reserved budget.

vikram: how do we avoid sampled retries creating DOS when upstream is degraded? backpressure still needs to be respected.

alex: agreed. sampled retries must be scoped by an ingress sampled-rate limiter and a per-tenant sampled-quota. sampled requests carry low priority and a specific header so upstream can deprioritize them.

jen: can you paste a minimal header contract?

alex: sure — proposal:
```
X-Retry-Sample: 1               # boolean flag for sampled retry
X-Retry-Sample-Prob: 0.05      # configured sampling probability
X-Sample-Id: <uuid>            # for dedupe / tracing
X-Retry-Priority: sampled      # hints to queueing/priority systems
X-Retry-Source: edge           # origin of the retry (edge|client|gateway)
```

marta: where do we count these for telemetry and SLOs? edge only or include upstream?

vikram: both. edge should increment sampled-retry counters and emit aggregated events. upstream should echo `X-Sample-Id` in spans so the tracing pipeline can dedupe work and measure end-to-end cost.

jen: what's the expected cost vs latency tradeoff? we can't just double work for small wins.

alex: early estimates: with 5% sampling we expect <1% extra token/time cost overall, but a measurable p99 reduction on noisy backends (5–15% improvement for affected calls). We'll tighten or disable sampling if cost drift exceeds threshold.

marta: rollout plan? we need a safe ramp.

alex: phased rollout: 1) telemetry-only mode (emit what would have been sampled) 2) enable sampled retries in staging with 0.5% prob 3) canary customers at 1–2% with opt-in config 4) global at 5% with auto-shed and tenant opt-out.

vikram: add explicit opt-out header so customers can block sampled retries: `X-Retry-Sample-Disable: 1`. also need tenant-level toggle in control plane.

jen: add audit log entries for sampled retries (important for side-effect safety and chargeback).

alex: yep — audit payload will include `X-Sample-Id`, tenant, route, and decision_reason. we'll surface sampled retry counts in console and per-route metrics.

marta: what about idempotency/side-effects? we should never allow sampled retries to hit unsafe routes unless a dedupe/guard exists.

alex: agreed. default: only allow sampled retries on routes declared idempotent or with an explicit side-effect-safe header from the client. otherwise sample-only in telemetry mode.

vikram: need to define how circuit-breakers treat sampled requests. my vote: CBs account them separately and allow low-volume sampled attempts (so they don't shorten circuit lifetimes), but if upstream signals overload we'll drop sampled retries first.

jen: also add a dashboard: sampled_retry_rate, sampled_success_rate, sampled_cost_delta, p99_improvement_by_route.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary-config/sampled-retries v1 -> staging :rocket:

alex: I'll draft an RFC with headers, control-plane flags, rollout steps, and dashboard mockups. I'll include AB test hypothesis and the metric thresholds for automatic rollback.

marta: +1 from infra, please include quota accounting so finance can attribute cost to tenants if sampling is enabled.

vikram: +1 from runtime, enforce per-host and per-tenant caps at ingress to prevent amplification.

alex: thanks — will send RFC and schedule a quick sync next week. :thumbsup:
